newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Group says Bosnian elections were mishandled.
newsitem.headline: Group says Bosnian elections were mishandled.

text.p: A private group monitoring the peace process in Bosnia said on Wednesday the international community had mishandled the allocation of seats after landmark elections in the former Yugoslav republic.

The International Crisis Group (ICG) said rules governing the way seats were allocated as a result of last month's elections had been changed without any announcement being made by the international electoral commission running the poll.
The September 14 poll elected national and regional assemblies -- both of which the ICG said had been affected by the change in rules -- and a three-man presidency.

The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), charged with supervising elections as part of the 1995 accord which ended 43 months of war in Bosnia, said it was looking into the problem urgently but denied any misallocation of seats.
The ICG said, however, the effect of the rule change had been to benefit the main nationalist parties, which emerged as winners, and to disadvantage smaller opposition parties.
"The new formula clearly boosts the nationalist parties," said ICG spokesman Chris Bennett.
"The opposition parties believe there was no consultation," he told reporters. In one case, the main Serb SDS party had gained two seats as a result of the new allocation method.
Bennett said the official election guidelines explained how seats should be allocated, but also contained a clause which made it impossible to allocate seats in certain circumstances.
The Provisional Elections Commission, an OSCE body, had therefore come up with a complex formula to get around the problem, but had not consulted with all parties, Bennett said.
The OSCE, which certified the September 14 elections at the end of last month, promised an urgent review of the matter but denied that as many as 30 seats could be affected.
"Certainly we are aware of the problem," said OSCE spokesman David Foley. "I'm sorry that I am not prepared to give the complete answer right now."
He told a news conference: "I will be prepared to make a complete statement on this issue very soon. We have it urgently under review to make sure we have all our ducks in a row on this issue."
Asked if the wrong seats had been allocated in some circumstances, Foley said: "Absolutely not, but I'm afraid I'm not prepared to go into it in any more depth now."
At a meeting on Tuesday with political parties, Robert Frowick, chairman of the OSCE mission to Bosnia, said that while the election process was not perfect, it would have to suffice.

Frowick was quoted by the Bosnian ONASA news agency as saying the formula for allocating seats was as complicated as "Einstein's theory of relativity" and that although there were "small errors that needed adjusting", there had been no significant vote-counting errors.
Municipal elections, seen as even more politically sensitive than last month's polls, will be held on November 22-24.
